### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a885324de7aece53599367c9e2546c992f07e2d` — the merge of head `ba1977cb24eb0f34a1dff1b7237958f11618885e` into base `d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a885324de7aece53599367c9e2546c992f07e2d && git checkout 2a885324de7aece53599367c9e2546c992f07e2d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a ba1977cb24eb0f34a1dff1b7237958f11618885e && git checkout -B drift-repro d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a && git merge --no-ff ba1977cb24eb0f34a1dff1b7237958f11618885e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1d90b7062af18eda616f875f9efc1ffeaac645a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `249ec4c4895c48ae38d1333f9df55d9336b896ac`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (`setMany`, `refuseByWritePredicates`, `registerWritePredicate`, `effectiveEnvOverride`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts (`SettingsWritePredicateInput`, `envKeyOf`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts (PUT locale), packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/localization-currency-lock.ts (the D4 precedent), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`getPublicConfig`, `isSsoWired`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/boot-sign-in-reachability.ts (`probeSsoProvidersPresence`, `SignInPathWiring`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-refusal-isolation.test.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsView.tsx (dirty-key save), .changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md

Inputs: card #30202 (body; comments 6648434001, 6648660209, 6650530417), PR #30298 body, file list and the net diff against `main` (merge base `4be97342`, 5 files, +641 / -0), and the check-runs on `249ec4c4`. Read-only: every file read with `git show` on the fetched ref; nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

- RIGHT — `PUT /api/settings/auth` and `SettingsService.setMany('auth', …)` now refuse `email_password_enabled: false` when the running `AuthManager` offers no other way in. The refusal rides the existing seam: `setMany` calls `refuseByWritePredicates` after `validatePatch` and before the crypto pass and every row write, so the whole batch is refused and nothing lands (the test's sibling `password_min_length` pin reads this correctly). The shape is the existing `SettingsValidationError` → `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `error.details.fields[]` one ADR-0114 field error `{ field, code: 'invalid_value', label, message, constraint: { lastSignInMethod } }`. No new code, key or export; the module is not re-exported from the package barrel. The declared "narrowing, nothing widened" is accurate for the surface.
- RIGHT — "re-saving the value in force is never refused": `refuseByWritePredicates` skips a key whose `stableStringify(next)` equals the cascade-resolved `current`; the console posts only `dirtyKeys` (`SettingsView.tsx:342`). So a deployment already in the dead-end state (stored `false`, nothing else) is NOT trapped: an unrelated auth key saves, re-posting `email_password_enabled: false` is skipped, and saving Google credentials while email and password is off is accepted (the Google-side predicate returns early when Google is not yet in force). Not pinned by a test, but read true.
- RIGHT — clearing / restore-default: `next` arrives as `null`; `readToggle(null, true)` is true for both toggles (manifest defaults are `true`), so clearing `email_password_enabled` or `google_enabled` is never refused; clearing a Google credential is judged against the apply's own fallbacks (`asTrimmedString(values.x) ?? env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_*`, and `configuredSocialProviders.google` which already includes the env-fallback Google from `applyEnvSocialProviderFallbacks`). `removesGoogle` mirrors the apply at `auth-plugin.ts` ~2365-2392 exactly, including `google_enabled: false` deleting a stack-declared Google.
- RIGHT — env-forced email/password: `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED` is `envKeyOf('auth','email_password_enabled')`, and `setMany` throws `SettingsLockedError` for a key whose env override is in force before any predicate runs, so an env-forced ON with a stored OFF never reaches the floor; the recovery path (env wins over the stored `false`, pinned in case 7) is the existing override. `OS_AUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED` is likewise the settings env name for `google_enabled`, so the apply's `googleEnabledFromEnv` and the floor can never disagree on a write (the write is locked).
- RIGHT — the list of other sign-in methods matches what the running manager serves, with two qualifications below: `getPublicConfig().socialProviders` (social entries with `enabled !== false`, plus OIDC entries, the same array the login page and the boot report's `SignInPathWiring.socialSignIn` read); `features.sso` = `isSsoWired()` (`plugins.sso ?? OS_SSO_ENABLED`) AND a `sys_sso_provider` row via `probeSsoProvidersPresence` (`'unknown'` on an unusable or throwing engine, read as absent — fail-safe); `features.phoneNumber` = `plugins.phoneNumber ?? false`; `hostSignInHandoff` from the option alone. Magic link and passkeys are not advertised by the login page and correctly do not count; `ssoOnlyMode` alone correctly does not count (its own contract keeps `emailPassword.enabled` true as break-glass).
- QUALIFICATION (should-fix, ④-3) — a social provider is counted on `enabled !== false` alone; `getPublicConfig` never checks that `clientId` / `clientSecret` resolve, so a stack-config provider whose credentials are blank (an unset env read in `objectstack.config.ts`) counts as a way in and lets email and password go off. The boot report's `socialSignIn` doc says "credentials present" but reads the same array, so the floor is consistent with the boot report; both are weaker than the claim.
- QUALIFICATION (not re-verified) — that better-auth's `/sign-in/phone-number` ignores `emailAndPassword.enabled` is the PR's claim; no `node_modules` is present on this checkout and the review is read-only, so it is taken as consistent with the plugin's shape, not proven here.
- WRONG — the predicate's claim "a change that would leave no way to sign in is refused" does not hold for a batch that removes two methods at once. See ④-1: it is the card's lockout, reachable in ONE save from the same Setup page.

Tests (11 cases, real `SettingsService` + `AuthPlugin` + `AuthManager`, dist-free since service-settings is aliased to src): they pin the single-key refusals, the HTTP envelope and locale, each counted method, the SSO-switch-alone and unreadable-table cases, the Google direction, the env-still-supplies case and the recovery override. They pin NO multi-key batch: neither the declared over-refusal (Google filled in and the switch off together) nor the both-off batch below. The `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` row is the ledger entry the gate requires for the test's `findOne` double — mechanical, correct.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`; title `fix(plugin-auth)!: …` (the `!` present on PR title and changeset); `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …` banner; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason. Under AGENTS.md's level rule (Post-Task Checklist 3) a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition: the level is right and justified. The `Check Changeset` and all `Lint` check-runs on this head are `success`, so the lines parse.
- Declaration lines PR body vs changeset: the value tokens are identical (`no (narrowing)`; `none`). The trailing prose on the `Clause-②:` line is NOT byte-identical — the PR body adds "; the new module is not exported from the package." The reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) judges the value class and tolerates decoration, so this parses on both carriers; noted, no finding.
- The changeset's Before / Now text overstates the enforcement (see ④-1) and omits the two-saves limitation the PR body declares; the CHANGELOG sentence an upgrading agent greps must say what the door actually refuses. Folded into ④-1's fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation 1 (`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the claimed surface): accepted — one ledger row the gate requires for a new test file with an engine double, nothing else in the file moves.
- Deviation 2 (refusal message names what to configure, not the recovery variable): accepted — the reader is the signed-in administrator; the variable is in the changeset.
- Deviations 3-4 (harness assign step skipped per order; only the 18 changeset-derived families re-run after the changeset-only commit): accepted; CI on this head is the authority and its gate-carrying runs are green or still running (see verdict).
- Dev flag "other doors to the same lockout" (deleting the last `sys_sso_provider` row, a redeploy dropping the last provider): out of this card's door, correctly noted, not a defect here.
- OPEN QUESTION — "a provider filled in and email and password turned off in the same save is refused; two saves acceptable?" Dev recommends A (keep). Judged against the card text ("The save is refused while it would leave no sign-in method"): the predicate evaluates each key against the RUNNING manager config (`deps.publicConfig()`) — not the post-save state of the batch, and not even the stored state. Over-refusal (A's friction): a batch `{ google_enabled, google_client_id, google_client_secret, email_password_enabled: false }` would NOT leave the deployment without a sign-in method, yet is refused; the mirror `{ email_password_enabled: true, google_enabled: false }` while email is off and Google last is refused too, with a message telling the admin to do the very thing the batch does. On its own that is a should-fix (fail-safe, declared, message explains). But the same per-key-against-live reading also UNDER-refuses — ④-1 — and that is the card's defect, so A is not acceptable as the resolution: the batch must be visible to the judgment. Option B (the batch on `SettingsWritePredicateInput`, an additive service-settings contract change, `Clause-②: yes`) or an equivalent whole-batch seam is required, in this PR or as a blocking prerequisite the card stays open on. Verdict on the question: A is a defect against the card — must-fix, because of ④-1; the over-refusal half alone would have been should-fix.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it makes the spec's own refusal real at the right door (the ADR-0144 D4 write predicate, the same seam `localization.currency` uses; before any write; the console already renders the field error), takes no declared capability away from the login page or `/auth/config`, and registers at `kernel:ready` so no boot-time seed or `recordApiKeyPolicyStart` write ever meets it (no non-test `setMany` caller exists outside the routes; `set` delegates to `setMany`). The scenarios tried:

1. MUST-FIX — both toggles off in one save is accepted and locks everyone out. Patch `{ email_password_enabled: false, google_enabled: false }` (or `google_client_secret: null` in place of the toggle) on a deployment whose only ways in are email/password and Google: `refuseByWritePredicates` asks the `email_password_enabled` predicate, which reads the LIVE `socialProviders`, sees Google, returns undefined; it then asks the `google_enabled` predicate, which reads the LIVE `emailPassword.enabled === true` at `sign-in-method-floor.ts:218` and returns undefined. Both rows are written; the apply pass turns email and password off and `delete socialProviders.google` (auth-plugin ~2384) — no sign-in method, "Settings saved". Both toggles sit on the same Authentication page and `SettingsView` posts all dirty keys in one PUT, so this is one click away in the card's own scenario ("moving to SSO, turn the local methods off"). The changeset's "a change that would leave no way to sign in is refused" is then a claim the runtime does not deliver (Prime Directive 10). Fix: judge the batch as a whole (option B above: hand the predicate the patch, or ask one batch-level predicate per namespace), and pin both batch shapes — the both-off batch refused, and the provider-plus-switch batch accepted — in `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`; then make the changeset's Now paragraph say exactly what is refused.
2. HOLDS — env-forced email/password with a stored OFF: the write is `SETTINGS_LOCKED` before the predicate; recovery override pinned (case 7).
3. SHOULD-FIX — SSO on with no provider rows: refused, correct. A Google (or any social) entry with empty credentials: counted, because `getPublicConfig` lists on `enabled !== false` alone. Read the credential pair where the floor counts a stack-declared provider (the same gap sits in the boot report's `socialSignIn`), or state in the module doc that a declared provider counts whether or not its credentials resolve. Low: the settings-managed Google path already requires both credentials to resolve before it is in force.
4. HOLDS — restore-default / clearing: `null` reads as the manifest default (`true`) for both toggles; credential clears follow the apply's env and stack fallbacks (pinned: env still supplies the secret → accepted, nothing removed).
5. HOLDS — seeded settings at boot: the predicate is registered inside `bindAuthSettings` at `kernel:ready` and never refuses a read or an apply; a stored `false` from before the floor still rules at boot (pinned as the control in case 7), so no boot, seed or import is broken.
6. HOLDS — already-locked deployment saving an unrelated auth key: predicates run only on patched floor keys whose value changes; Google credentials can be added while email is off; the admin is not trapped.
7. SHOULD-FIX (test) — the declared limitation ("two saves") is not pinned; once ④-1 is fixed, the accepted provider-plus-switch batch is the pin that replaces it.

Must-fix 1 is a FAIL. Check-runs on `249ec4c4`, read 2026-11-05T05:44Z: 30 `success` (every `Lint` job, `Check Changeset`, every `Type Check` job, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 5-8 among them), 13 `skipped` (UI and opt-in lanes, no `ui/` paths), and `Test Core` 1-4 still `in_progress` at the end of the review's ten-minute polling window; none red. The verdict does not rest on them: ④-1 fails it on the tree.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b89bdf1dd9a83ee5aae5a83ec80f5dd0de8a61c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-write-predicate.test.ts, .changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts (PUT, `dropEchoedSecretMasks`, locale), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-secret-redaction.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts (`scope: 'global'`, the four floor keys, `google_client_secret` encrypted), packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts (the type's re-export on `main`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`getPublicConfig`: social ids, `oidc` entries keyed `providerId`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/boot-sign-in-reachability.ts (`probeSsoProvidersPresence`); for the compose flag, PR #30309 at `8767d6aa` (`settings-service.ts`, `settings-service.types.ts`, `index.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`)

Delta review of the re-fix after record 6650756385 (FAIL on `249ec4c4`). Inputs: card #30202 body and every comment (6648434001, 6648660209, 6650530417, 6650553927, 6652019341), PR #30298 body as it stands, file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `c1240a38`, 8 files, +886 / -3, identical against current `origin/main` `8c9f48f8`), the delta `249ec4c4..0b89bdf1`, record 6650756385, and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: every file read with `git show` on the fetched ref; nothing built, run or re-run. The one script run was `record-recognisers.mjs --template`, which reads no board.

The delta is two commits on the first-parent line: the fix `5cc78ec5` (7 files, +316 / -74) and the merge `0b89bdf1` of `main` `c1240a38` (which carries `977be380`, `fccde75e`, `c1240a38` and their ancestors). `git diff 5cc78ec5 0b89bdf1` restricted to the PR's eight paths is empty, and `git diff 4be97342 c1240a38` on the same eight paths is empty: the merge touches no path of this PR, and the 73 other files in the delta stat are `main`'s own (the Feature Flags removal in service-settings translations, ui hitl work, record timeline). The ledger row in `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` is unchanged since `249ec4c4`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes of the delta, each judged against the cited code:

- RIGHT — `SettingsWritePredicateInput` gains `batch`, optional, typed as a readonly record of string to unknown, with TSDoc. `refuseByWritePredicates` builds it once per call, from the whole `patch` (`submitted ?? null`, so a cleared key is `null`), `Object.freeze`s it, and passes the same object to every predicate it asks. It is additive: `localization-currency-lock.ts` ignores it, and a hand-built input omits it. The type was already re-exported from the package entry on `main` (`index.ts:59`), so "reachable from `@objectstack/service-settings`" is true without an `index.ts` change; the `expectTypeOf` case imports it from `./index.js`. The declared "widening half" names exactly this, nothing more.
- RIGHT — the floor now judges the post-save state. `signInMethodFloorPredicate` reads `batch` (falling back to `{ [key]: next }` for a host that passes none), takes `email_password_enabled` after the save from the batch when the save sets it, else from the running manager; `googleAfter` applies the same rule `bindAuthSettings` applies (`auth-plugin.ts` ~2371-2397): off when `google_enabled` is off; else a stack-declared Google counts only with its boot credential pair; else in force with a client ID and secret each from the batch, the stored value (`SettingsService.get`, which decrypts in-process, `materialiseRow`), or the `GOOGLE_CLIENT_*` variable. A save that sets no `google_*` key leaves Google as it stands. The must-fix batch `{ email_password_enabled: false, google_enabled: false }` on email+Google: the email key sees Google gone after the save and refuses; the Google key sees email off after the save, Google in force now, nothing else, Google gone after, and refuses. Two field errors, nothing written. Pinned at test lines 188-207 for both batch shapes (`google_enabled: false` and `google_client_secret: null`); the accepted batches (Google filled in with the switch off; the switch turned on over a stored pair) at 209-226; the half-pair batch refused at 228-239. Ablations D and E (no batch passed; floor ignores batch) each red those pins per the report; not re-run here.
- RIGHT — the prior record's over-refusal mirror (`{ email_password_enabled: true, google_enabled: false }` while email was off and Google last) is now accepted: `emailPasswordAfter` is read from the batch as `true` and both keys return early. Not pinned by name; read true.
- RIGHT — a social or OIDC provider counts only with a credential pair. `providerCredentialIndex` is built in `init` after `applyEnvSocialProviderFallbacks` and the `auth:configure` trigger, from the resolved `authConfig.socialProviders` / `oidcProviders`, keyed `social:id` and `oidc:providerId`; `getPublicConfig` emits social entries under their config key and OIDC entries with `id: p.providerId`, so the lookup keys match. A blank or whitespace secret is "no pair" (`trim() !== ''`). Pinned at 241-249 (stack GitHub with a blank secret is refused) and 251-265 (the index itself). The boot report's `socialSignIn` keeps the weaker reading; the floor no longer depends on it.
- RIGHT — the `providerHasCredentials` default for a provider absent from the boot index is `true`, which is what makes the settings-added Google count (the apply adds it only with both credentials). See ④-4 for its breadth.
- RIGHT — "re-saving the value in force is never refused" still holds: `refuseByWritePredicates` skips a key whose `stableStringify(next)` equals the resolved current before asking; the batch still carries that key, so a predicate asked about another key sees the full post-save picture. An unchanged secret never reaches the batch from the console: the PUT route drops an echoed mask (`dropEchoedSecretMasks`) before `setMany`, so the floor reads it as stored.
- RIGHT — declaration completeness: "No new error code or settings key" true; the module is still not re-exported from the plugin-auth barrel; the `auth` manifest is `scope: 'global'`, so the acceptance note about organization-scope fallback names a case the namespace cannot reach.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch` and `'@objectstack/service-settings': patch`; title `fix(plugin-auth)!:` with the `!`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (one arm from the closed pair); `Metadata-protocol: none`; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, its reason now naming the additive `batch` field; the `**BREAKING**` banner once. Under Post-Task Checklist 3 a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition: both levels are right (ruling A).
- The two declaration lines are byte-identical between the PR body and the changeset (checked by digest of each first `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol:` line). `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.
- The changeset's Now / "The whole save is judged" / "What counts" paragraphs now say what the door refuses, including the two-field refusal and the credential-pair rule; the sentence an upgrading agent greps matches the runtime.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Must-fix ④-1 of 6650756385 (both toggles off in one save accepted): CLOSED, on the tree and by pin (①, lines 188-207), through the seat's ruling B seam.
- Should-fix ④-3 (provider counted without credentials): CLOSED (①, lines 241-265).
- Should-fix ④-7 (the two-saves limitation unpinned): CLOSED by replacement, the accepted-batch pins at 209-226.
- Open question of 6650530417 (A vs B): resolved B, as ruled; the dev's report 6652019341 declares the `service-settings` surface as the seat-ordered deviation and the PR body rewrite as the seat's. Accepted.
- Dogfood: on `0b89bdf1`, 4 cases of `packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts` timed out at 5000 ms while 73 gate families ran beside the battery; the same file alone under the lock passed 12/12.
